lead: A transmitter turns digital baseband samples into an RF signal at the antenna with enough power, in the correct band, and without spreading into neighbouring channels. It mirrors the receiver: filters, mixers and amplifiers return, but power and spectral mask now dominate. The same local oscillator and duplexer are often shared with the receiver, so transmit leakage and loss affect both sides. Direct upconversion is common in phones and Wi-Fi. Two-step upconversion survives where sharper filtering of spurs is needed. This chapter builds the chain and its numbers.
prereq: You need: receiver chain (5.4), mixer up/down conversion (5.7), and antenna gain/EIRP (Unit 2).

blocks.text: Digital baseband produces two streams, I and Q. The DAC converts each stream to an analog voltage. A reconstruction filter after the DAC removes sampling images. The I/Q modulator multiplies I by cos(2πf_LO t) and Q by sin(2πf_LO t), then adds them. Here f_LO is the local-oscillator frequency and t is time. With ideal gain and 90° phase, the two paths cancel the unwanted sideband and place the signal at f_LO. The driver amplifier raises the level to the PA input. The PA sets output power. A harmonic filter after the PA suppresses 2f_LO, 3f_LO and higher components. A duplexer, or a TDD switch, connects the PA to the antenna while protecting the receiver. The antenna radiates the RF wave.

Two-step upconversion uses two mixers: baseband to IF with f_IF, an IF filter, then IF to RF with f_LO2. It costs more parts but gives sharper filtering of spurs and images. Direct upconversion avoids the IF filter and is smaller; it needs good I/Q matching.

The transmitter must radiate inside its assigned channel and stay quiet outside. A spectral mask is a regulatory limit on power versus frequency offset from the carrier. It is an absolute curve, not a ratio. ACLR stands for adjacent-channel leakage ratio. Some syllabi call the same quantity ACPR, adjacent-channel power ratio. ACLR is the ratio of power in the wanted channel to power in the adjacent channel, in dBc. A good ACLR is a large number, for example 45 dBc, meaning the adjacent channel is 45 dB below the wanted one. Nonlinearity in the PA broadens the spectrum and raises adjacent power. I/Q gain or phase error also creates an image and worsens the mask.

blocks.where: EIRP is equivalent isotropic radiated power; P_PA is the power at the output of the power amplifier, before the harmonic filter and duplexer; L_feed is the loss of the harmonic filter, duplexer or switch and any cable between the PA and the antenna; G_ant is the antenna gain in dBi relative to an isotropic radiator. Count L_feed once, on the transmit path. If you already know the power at the antenna port, write EIRP_dBm = P_ant,dBm + G_ant,dBi and add no loss term.

sections.h3: Shared hardware: LO, duplexer and TDD switch

blocks.text: A transceiver shares hardware. One synthesizer can feed the RX and TX mixers. Sharing saves area and power, but the TX LO can leak into the RX mixer, and a strong TX signal can couple into the LNA. The duplexer provides isolation, yet its loss appears in both directions. On transmit, duplexer loss reduces EIRP by the same number of dB. On receive, the same loss adds directly to the receiver noise figure and reduces sensitivity. Do not count it once for both. In FDD, the duplexer has a transmit band filter and a receive band filter; its loss is typically 1–3 dB in a handset. In TDD, a switch replaces the duplexer. The switch has insertion loss and finite isolation; it must disconnect the PA before the LNA is connected. A guard period covers switching time. Poor isolation lets the PA burn the LNA or desensitize it. The shared LO also needs good phase noise, because phase noise on TX spreads the spectrum and on RX transfers to the downconverted signal.

figure.caption: A direct-conversion transmitter: the shared local oscillator drives the I/Q modulator; a reconstruction filter cleans the DAC output and a harmonic filter after the PA suppresses 2f_LO and 3f_LO. The PA, duplexer and antenna set output power and EIRP. Duplexer loss lies in both the transmit and receive paths.

spec.title: Direct-conversion transmitter
spec.aria: A direct-conversion transmitter chain from baseband through DAC, reconstruction filter, I/Q modulator, PA, harmonic filter, duplexer and antenna, with a shared local oscillator feeding the modulator.

examples.question: A direct-conversion transmitter delivers 0 dBm at the I/Q modulator output. The PA has 25 dB gain and an output 1-dB compression point P1dB,out = 26 dBm. The harmonic filter and duplexer together have 2 dB loss. The antenna gain is 3 dBi. Find the PA output, the power at the antenna port, the EIRP and the PA back-off from P1dB,out.
steps: Convert the modulator output to dBm: P_mod = 0 dBm.
Add PA gain: P_PA = P_mod + G_PA = 0 dBm + 25 dB = 25 dBm. This is the PA output.
Subtract filter and duplexer loss: P_ant = P_PA − L_feed = 25 dBm − 2 dB = 23 dBm at the antenna port.
Add antenna gain: EIRP = P_ant + G_ant = 23 dBm + 3 dBi = 26 dBm. The same result comes from P_PA − L_feed + G_ant.
Compare with P1dB,out: back-off = P1dB,out − P_PA = 26 dBm − 25 dBm = 1 dB. The PA is 1 dB below compression, so compression is small but not zero.
examples.answer: EIRP = 26 dBm, with PA output 25 dBm, antenna-port power 23 dBm and 1 dB back-off from P1dB,out.
examples.check:
p_mod_dbm = 0.0
pa_gain_db = 25.0
loss_db = 2.0
ant_gain_dbi = 3.0
p1db_out_dbm = 26.0
pa_out_dbm = p_mod_dbm + pa_gain_db
p_ant_dbm = pa_out_dbm - loss_db
eirp_dbm = p_ant_dbm + ant_gain_dbi
backoff_db = p1db_out_dbm - pa_out_dbm
print(f"{pa_out_dbm:.1f}")
print(f"{p_ant_dbm:.1f}")
print(f"{eirp_dbm:.1f}")
print(f"{backoff_db:.1f}")

traps: Do not multiply power in dBm by a gain in dB. Gains in dB add to power in dBm: 0 dBm + 25 dB = 25 dBm. Writing 0 dBm × 25 dB is meaningless; convert to mW first if you must multiply (1 mW × 316 = 316 mW = 25 dBm).
Duplexer loss is a loss on the TX path and again on the RX path. Count each path separately; never subtract it twice on one path.
EIRP uses antenna gain but not receiver gain. A 3 dBi antenna adds 3 dB to EIRP; an LNA gain belongs to the receive chain.
ACLR is a ratio in dBc; a larger dBc number means less adjacent leakage. A spectral mask is an absolute limit in dBm or dBm/Hz at a frequency offset.
P1dB,out is an output power, not a gain. Back-off is P1dB,out minus the actual PA output in dBm; the result is in dB.

quiz.q: State the EIRP formula for a transmitter.
quiz.a: EIRP_dBm = P_PA,dBm − L_feed,dB + G_ant,dBi, where P_PA is the power at the PA output and L_feed is the loss of the filter, duplexer or switch and cables between the PA and the antenna. Starting instead at the antenna port, EIRP_dBm = P_ant,dBm + G_ant,dBi with no loss term.

quiz.q: Why does a shared LO save hardware but need isolation?
quiz.a: One synthesizer feeds both RX and TX mixers, saving area and power; TX LO or signal can leak into the RX and desensitize it.

quiz.q: A PA gives 20 dBm. Filter loss is 1.5 dB and antenna gain is 2 dBi. Find EIRP.
EIRP is met but the spectral mask fails. Give two likely causes and one fix.
quiz.a: PA compression or I/Q mismatch; fix with more back-off, digital predistortion, or I/Q trim.

quiz.q: Define ACLR and give its unit.
quiz.a: Ratio of wanted-channel power to adjacent-channel power; unit dBc.

quiz.q: Why does duplexer loss reduce receiver sensitivity?
quiz.a: It adds loss before the LNA, raising the receiver noise figure.

quiz.q: PA P1dB,out = 30 dBm, actual output 28 dBm. Find back-off.
TDD switch isolation is poor. What happens at the receiver?
quiz.a: TX leakage enters the LNA, causing compression or blocking; more isolation and a guard period are needed.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern phones use transceiver SoCs with shared synthesizers, digital predistortion and envelope tracking to keep PA efficiency high while meeting ACLR. 5G massive MIMO puts many transmit chains behind one array, so per-element EIRP and leakage matter. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth integrate TDD switches on chip. Search terms: direct-conversion transmitter, ACLR, spectral mask, duplexer, TX leakage, digital predistortion.
